content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents an Inverse Optimal Control (IOC) method that utilizes a triangle inequality based constraint on the value function to estimate a better representation of the cost function. The method builds on top of prior work that models IOC as a constrained optimization problem that recovers a polynomial approximation of the cost function subject to an epsilon relaxation of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation and a unit-sum constraint on the polynomial coefficients. By adding an extra constraint that the cost of any route that traverses a waypoint not on the optimal path is greater than or equal to the cost of the optimal path, i.e. a triangle inequality, this problem can be additional constrained. The method proposes a way to integrate this into the prior IOC formulation through the use of a reverse-time value function and derives the updated optimization problem under this added constraint. This approach is tested on four different problems; three of these are with polynomial system dynamics, cost and one is with a 2-link manipulator whose dynamics are not polynomial. Additionally, some of the tested problems have time-dependent costs. The approach performs better compared to the prior baseline at approximating the underlying true cost function and recovering the optimal behavior when working with a single or multiple expert demonstrations.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
(+) The paper is clearly written and explained. The method is well described in the text, and even with the large amount of mathematical notation and equations the message gets clearly across. I particularly like how the math was explained in the text which made it easy to understand the overall approach.

(+) The approach gets good results on a variety of toy problems and performs better compared to the baseline approach upon which it builds.

(+) There is a nice discussion section which summarizes some of the challenges of the proposed method and outlines directions for future work. 

(-) The approach has only been tested on very simple toy problems, and while the results are good it seems hard to scale the constrained optimization style method to larger state and action spaces.

(-) The key novelty in the approach is the introduction of the triangle inequality as an additional constraint for the value function. For tasks of a spatial nature where there is a single optima for a given problem instance it seems like this would help but does the general principle scale past these kinds of "spatial" tasks? What about tasks where the underlying expert demonstrations can be multi-modal?

(-) A key drawback of the proposed approach is the need for a separate reverse value function estimation for each trajectory with a different start state. This linear scaling seems prohibitive as already shown in the time taken for computation given multiple trajectories (shown in the appendix results). Unless this is overcome there is no clear path to applying the approach to larger problems. A potential option to tackle this could be to estimate a single reverse value function that additionally takes as input the start state; i.e. make it a polynomial function in two variables. 

(-) There are no comparisons to other related IOC approaches other than the baseline upon which this approach builds on. It would be useful to compare to atleast a single other method (with a potential sweep over number of expert trajectories provided) to get an idea of the overall strengths of the proposed approach.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper is well written, and even with a lot of mathematical notation the explanation is well conveyed. The figures and results are well done, and clearly highlight the strengths of the proposed approach.

Quality & Novelty: The key novelty of the proposed approach is in the addition of the triangle inequality as extra constraints for cost function optimization. This is well teased out in the paper. There are some drawbacks of the proposed method, specifically, the linear increase in computation time make it hard to scale. Additionally, the approach has only been tested on very simple toy problems.

Reproducibility: The approach is explained clearly & the tasks and expert policies used for evaluation are clearly explained in the paper. The approach does seem a bit tricky to reproduce as it uses MATLAB, a closed source package. There was a github link with the code provided which could have helped with reproducibility but this link does not work.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper presented an IOC method that leverages an additional triangle inequality based constraint to recover a better representation of the cost/value function from expert demonstrations. The approach is described clearly and tested on a set of simple toy problems where it shows good performance compared to a prior baseline. There are some drawbacks specifically regarding the simplicity of the evaluation and computational complexity of the proposed method that need to be addressed.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose a new inverse optimal control (IOC) method leveraging the triangle inequality in the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations. The authors base their method on a linear programming baseline where the value function is optimized with the HJB equation posed as the constraints. On top of the baseline, the authors further include the triangle inequality of the cost path integral as additional constraints to further regularize the optimization. The proposed IOC method is tested on a few hypothetical systems and a realistic two link arm setup, and shows better performance (less errors) in cost learning.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1, The proposed method is a simple enough modification and can be easily implemented for various systems.
2, The proposed method demonstrates better cost learning and expert trajectory tracking performances.  
 
Weaknesses:
1, The paper seems to only be compared with one baseline method (which the proposed method modified from). 
2, The studied systems are mostly hypothetical or simple (i.e. 2-link arms). It is unclear if the proposed method can be applied to real world systems with more complex inputs (such as high DoF robots or multi modalities).
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is easy to follow, but the originality is limited (i.e. a relatively simple modification to an existing method). The evaluation set is OK but there is only one IOC baseline being compared to.
content.summary_of_the_review: I actually think this paper might fits better for venues like L4DC than ICLR.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
